note: Track steps-to-leaps, mix step 8 (steps and skips in one tune): one rising ear game narrowed with "set" to a step, both 3rds, the 5th and the 6th, where both notes are sung back on "oo" before each answer; the answers are named as the game's buttons show them, and the one care line keeps the singer off the high notes. Folds in the five-intervals-sung-back copy, whose set this is.

exercise.title: Hear and sing back
exercise.why: Singing the two notes back makes your voice find the distance your ear just heard, which is how a tune is learned by ear.

cells.text:
Press Start in the game below to hear two notes, the second one higher. Sing both back on "oo", then pick the interval's name: M2 for a step (a major 2nd), m3 or M3 for a minor or major 3rd, P5 for a 5th or M6 for a major 6th.
_Don't reach for high notes: start the pair lower when the top note feels tight._
Practice until your voice lands on the second note straight away, without sliding up to it.
